Hi Sara — attaching the SDK quickstart and a sample model-routing policy. High-level notes below; see attachments for full files: redwood_sdk_quickstart.md, model-routing-sample.yaml

Auth & SDK options:
- Hosted (Redwood API):
  - API key for PoC and low-risk workloads. Short-lived keys supported via token exchange.
  - For additional assurance can enable mTLS+IP allowlist on dedicated accounts.
- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Client TLS (mTLS) + JWK token exchange to integrate with your KMS.
  - Customers can bring KMS/HSM; audit logs are emitted to your SIEM.

SDK Quickstart (curl + python snippets):
- curl example (hosted):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/llama-2-13b","input":"hello"}' \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

- python (structured output + tool call pattern):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
  resp = client.generate(model='redwood/chat-medium',\n                         input='Find customer 123 and return JSON {id,name,active}')
  # SDK supports structured output schema enforcement and tool-calling hooks

Model routing & policy (high-level):
- Policy primitives: latency_threshold_ms, cost_tier, region_preference, fallback_chain, allowed_models.
- Example (see model-routing-sample.yaml attachment) — sample explains:
  - Primary route: region: us-west, model: redwood/chat-low-latency, latency_threshold_ms: 200
  - Fallback: if latency > 200ms or model unavailable -> redwood/chat-cost-optimized (lower cost, lower perf)
  - Batch rerank route: region: us-east, policy: cost_tier: medium, model: redwood/reranker-cross-encoder-large (used for top-100 candidates only)

Policy considerations for your use-case:
- Use an inexpensive embedding model (redwood/embed-small) for vector indexing; use a cross-encoder reranker (redwood/rerank-large) for final scoring on a trimmed candidate set.
- Configure prefix/KV caching for chat to reduce token generation and hit latency targets for repeated prompts.
- Set automatic fallback to smaller model when latency spikes, but gate by a quality-monitoring hook — if QA drop > X% then alert and block fallback rollouts.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_quickstart.md (code + auth flows), model-routing-sample.yaml (policy examples).

Let me know if you want an annotated config during the deep-dive.

Sara — quick notes from an SE perspective on embeddings/reranker and routing behaviors: 

Embeddings + rerank topology:
- Recommend pipeline:
  1) Embed documents offline with redwood/embed-small (cost-effective).
  2) ANN index (e.g., Pinecone/FAISS) for candidate retrieval.
  3) Cross-encoder reranker (redwood/rerank-large) on top N=50-200 candidates to maximize precision.
- For throughput-sensitive endpoints, run reranker in a separate, batched worker pool to avoid blocking chat tokens.

Model routing & policy tips:
- Canary approach: route 95% to primary model in us-west, 5% to a candidate for quality comparison.
- Latency-based fallback: policy engine supports runtime latency metrics; define latency_threshold_ms and fallback_chain. Example: if p95 > 200ms over 1m window -> switch to fallback model in <30s.
- Region routing: implement sticky routing per user region. If primary region unavailable route to nearest fallback region and annotate the request with a region_fallback flag.

Structured output / tool calling:
- SDK supports structured-output schema enforcement (JSON Schema) and a tool-calling hook that executes registered webhooks (signed with mTLS).
- Pattern: model emits a structured payload with a tool call intent; middleware validates and forwards to internal API. We recommend a verification layer that enforces token-scoped permissions.

Performance & cost controls:
- Use batching for embeddings ingestion and cross-encoder reranks.
- Use token-cost monitoring per-route and set automated alerts for cost spikes.

Happy to walk through a sample traffic-based policy during the deep-dive. Attaching a short sample policy in the shared drive as well.

— Marcus
